javax.microedition.theme
Class Capabilities

java.lang.Object
  javax.microedition.theme.Capabilities

public class Capabilities
extends java.lang.Object

Returns static information about the capabilities of the Mobile User Interface Customization API implementation found in the device.

Methods in this class typically take as parameters a feature and a role, as found in elements. The methods always deal with top-level elements, not members of element groups.

getSupportedMediaTypes

public static java.lang.String[] getSupportedMediaTypes(java.lang.String feature,
                                                        java.lang.String role,
                                                        java.lang.String kind)
                                                 throws ElementNotFoundException

Gets the supported media types of the specified kind, for the base element with the specified feature and role. This method returns an array of java.lang.String instances containing the registered MIME type strings for media types supported for the particular kind.

For example, assume that feature="general" and role="screensaver", and the implementation supports as the screen saver one of the following: an animated GIF89a image, a PNG image, a 3GPP video clip or an M3G model. To find out the supported media types for this element, you will need to call this method once for each Element.KIND_xxx value. For the kind argument value Element.KIND_GRAPHIC this method would return an array of String instances with the following content:

{ "image/gif", "image/png", "application/m3g" }

For the kind argument value Element.KIND_VIDEO, it would return an array containing one element:

{ "video/3gpp" }

Note that since only the graphic, sound and video kinds can have associated media types, other Element.KIND_xxx constants used as the kind argument return an empty array. If the kind is not supported for the element, an empty array is returned.

This method can be used only with base elements supported by the implementation (i.e. elements for which isBaseElementSupported returns true). If the implementation does not support the base element with the specified feature and role, this method throws ElementNotFoundException.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
kind - one of the Element.KIND_xxx constants
Returns:
a string array of registered MIME type strings for the supplied kind, empty if registered MIME types do not apply to kind or the kind is not supported for the element
Throws:
ElementNotFoundException - if the base element with the specified feature and role is not supported by the implementation
java.lang.NullPointerException - if feature, role or kind is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if feature, role or kind is empty, or if kind is not one of those defined in the Element interface
See Also:
Element

isBaseElementSupported

public static boolean isBaseElementSupported(java.lang.String feature,
                                             java.lang.String role)

Determines if the element with the specified feature and role is supported or not as a base element. Because the customizable elements are conditionally mandatory, all base elements are not necessarily supported.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
Returns:
true if element is supported, false if not
Throws:
java.lang.NullPointerException - if feature is null or role is null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if feature or role is empty

isCustomizationPolicyEnabled

public static boolean isCustomizationPolicyEnabled()

Determines if a device has a customization policy enabled. Applications can call the isElementCustomizable method of this class to find out if a base element is customizable or not.

Returns:
true if customization policy enabled, false if not
See Also:
isElementCustomizable(String, String)

isElementCustomizable

public static boolean isElementCustomizable(java.lang.String feature,
                                            java.lang.String role)
                                     throws ElementNotFoundException

Determines if the base element with the specified feature and role is customizable according to the effective device customization policy.

If the isCustomizationPolicyEnabled method returns false, this method must return true.

If the customization of an element group is not customizable, all the child elements of the group must be implicitly not customizable.

Parameters:
feature - the feature of the element
role - the role of the element
Returns:
true if base element is customizable, false if not
Throws:
ElementNotFoundException - if the implementation does not support this feature and role combination
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if any parameter is empty
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
See Also:
isCustomizationPolicyEnabled()
